Handover document

FitAI — project delivery and future scope

Your fitness. Your data. Your AI coach.

Delivery and future scope · version 1.0 · 29 October 2026

Team: Gourav Narvariya (lead) · FitAI hackathon squad Repo: github.com/gouravN0709/Hackathon-2-Gourav-Narvariya Live URL: configure on Vercel (not stored in repo)

Executive summary

What we promised vs what shipped

The MVP committed to a member-facing web app: auth and onboarding, a data-rich dashboard, workout planner and logger, nutrition tracking, progress analytics, and Nova as an AI coach—all on a premium dark UI with PWA support. That scope is implemented and covered by automated tests. Nova uses a deterministic keyword engine tied to live user data, not a hosted LLM yet. Supabase replaces the original local-only persistence plan while keeping the same screens and copy.

Vision and problem

Who we are solving for

Member pain points

No clear plan

Unsure what to train each day or how to progress loads.

Nutrition guesswork

Hard to hit protein and calories without a simple log.

Invisible progress

Weight and strength trends live in scattered notes.

Generic advice

Content that ignores actual workouts and meals.

Fragmented tools

Separate apps for lifting, food, and chat.

Motivation drops

No timely, personal nudges when consistency slips.

Trainer and gym operator pain points

Manual programming

Plans rebuilt from scratch for every client.

Blind spots

Limited view of who actually trained and ate on plan.

Churn

Engagement falls when digital touchpoints are weak.

Commodity floor

Hard to differentiate without connected member data.

Demo tour

Screen-by-screen walkthrough

Screenshots: Playwright on production build (login, onboarding, help, offline) and visual-regression baselines at 1440 and 390 px (seeded demo data, frozen date 15 Oct 2026).

Login

Sign in or create an account with email and password. Validation, password visibility, and forgot-password flow match Brand OS copy.

  • Switch between log in and sign up without losing email
  • Submit with keyboard Enter
  • Success screen routes to dashboard or onboarding

Why it matters: Trust starts here—fast auth with clear errors before any data is collected.

Onboarding

Five steps capture stats, goal, experience, and diet, then show computed calorie and protein targets before the first dashboard visit.

  • Boundary validation on age, height, and weight
  • Single-select goal and diet cards
  • Plan builder animation then dashboard handoff

Why it matters: Every ring and Nova reply later depends on targets set once, correctly.

Dashboard

Home screen for today: rings, weight, workout status, and quick actions to food, progress, workout, and coach.

  • Quick actions deep-link to the right flow
  • Seven- and thirty-day weight toggle on desktop
  • Command palette from header or Ctrl/Cmd+K

Why it matters: One glance answers “what should I do next?”

AI coach (Nova)

Chat with suggested prompts, typing indicator, and a context panel reflecting live workout and nutrition state.

  • Prompt chips send curated questions
  • Replies stream word-by-word (UI); logic is keyword-based
  • Quick links back to dashboard, nutrition, or workouts

Why it matters: Coaching feels personal because numbers come from the member’s own logs—even before a real LLM ships.

Workouts — planner

  • Week strip with done / planned / rest states
  • Regenerate plan (rule-based RPC)
  • Custom routines and muscle filters

Why it matters: Structure beats random gym sessions.

Workouts — details and active

  • Start workout from details
  • Rest timer after each set; finish saves session to Supabase
  • Volume and minutes roll up to progress and dashboard

Why it matters: Logged sets become charts, PRs, and coach context automatically.

Nutrition and food search

  • Meal tabs and macro split bar
  • Search, serving multiplier, custom foods
  • Undo toast when removing items

Why it matters: Protein and calorie gaps close only when logging is fast.

Progress

  • Log weight with validation and undo
  • Weight, consistency, calorie trend, top lifts
  • Ask Nova about progress prefills coach chat

Why it matters: Trends beat single-day scale noise.

Profile and settings

  • Edit targets with unsaved-changes guard
  • Notifications, interface sounds, install app card
  • Feedback modal and demo reset

Why it matters: Members own their targets and how the app talks to them.

Help

  • Searchable topics from src/content/help.ts
  • InfoTips on charts and fields
  • Five-step coachmark tour on first visits

Why it matters: Reduces support load; every metric is explained in plain language.

Mobile and PWA

  • Bottom tab bar below 820 px; profile via avatar
  • Install banner after engagement; iOS share-sheet instructions
  • Service worker caches shell; offline page when navigation fails

Why it matters: Gyms have dead zones—installable offline shell keeps the product usable.

Data and security

What is stored where

Supabase Postgres

Profiles, weight logs, meals, sessions, chat messages, plans, feedback. User-scoped via RLS.

Browser

Query cache, offline queue, active workout in progress, PWA install dismissal, tour flags in profile settings JSON.

Catalog tables

Exercises, workouts, foods—read-only for signed-in users; seeded in migration 004.

Privacy: No third-party analytics in repo. Account delete cascades via service-role API. Help copy is being aligned with Supabase storage (some help topics still mention localStorage-only).

Demo script

Three to five minute live tour

0:00 · Introduction — “FitAI is a member app that turns your own workout and meal logs into a daily plan and a coach that cites your numbers. This is the MVP we shipped for the hackathon.”

0:30 · Problem — “Members juggle planners, macros, and generic tips. Trainers and gyms cannot see consistent data. We focused Phase 1 on the member.”

1:00 · Solution — “Sign up, five-step onboarding, then one dashboard for today’s workout, rings, and Nova.”

1:30 · Screen tour — Follow click path below.

4:00 · Conclusion — “MVP is test-green and deploy-ready on Supabase and Vercel. Nova is simulated today; Gemini and trainer tools are on the roadmap.”

Click path

  1. /login → demo alex@fitai.app (or sign up) → dashboard
  2. Dashboard → Start workout → details → active → complete one set → finish (optional short path)
  3. Dashboard → Nutrition → add food → return
  4. Coach → tap “Analyze my progress” → read Nova reply
  5. Progress → log weight → Profile → show install app / feedback
  6. Ctrl+K → “help” → Help center

Honest limits

Known limitations and risks

  • Nova is simulated — keyword engine, not Gemini; mitigated by clear UI and Phase 5 backlog.
  • No push notifications — by design in PWA plan; mitigated with in-app reminders toggles for future server push.
  • Demo seed fragility — local-only; catalog duplicate on db reset; mitigated by db:check-catalog-seed and apply-demo.sh guards.
  • Help privacy copy — partially outdated vs Supabase; mitigated by content pass on help.ts.
  • Live URL not in repo — set Vercel production URL before investor demos.

Future scope

Roadmap phases 2–6

Trainer platform

Goals: roster management, assign plans, view client logs. Features: trainer dashboard, client compliance, messaging. Depends on MVP + RBAC. Effort: M. Value: high for PT businesses.

Gym owner and admin

Goals: engagement analytics, staff roles, branded experience. Depends on Phase 2. Effort: M–L. Value: churn reduction.

Smart gym

Goals: equipment and check-in data tied to profiles. Depends on hardware partners. Effort: L. Value: premium differentiation.

Advanced AI and integrations

Goals: Gemini via server routes, weekly AI reports, wearables, push reminders. Depends on secrets + rate limits. Effort: M–L. Value: core moat.

Marketplace

Goals: sell programs and trainer services in-app. Depends on payments + moderation. Effort: L. Value: new revenue.

Near-term backlog

  • Real AI coach (Gemini via server)
  • Push reminders
  • Weekly AI reports
  • Offline sync improvements
  • Accessibility and performance hardening
  • Analytics and feedback loop (server ingest)

Next steps

Decisions needed: Confirm Vercel production URL; approve Gemini budget and data policy; prioritize Phase 2 vs Phase 5 AI.

  • 30 days: Wire Gemini server route behind feature flag; server-side feedback ingest; fix catalog seed duplication on db reset.
  • 60 days: Push notification provider; weekly email/AI summary; integration test suite in CI.
  • 90 days: Trainer MVP discovery; wearable import spike; marketplace feasibility study.

Support: run CI on main; rotate Supabase keys via dashboard; never run seed-demo on production.

Appendix

Glossary, FAQ, credits

Progressive overload — Gradually increase weight, reps, or volume over time.

BMR and TDEE — Basal metabolic rate and total daily energy expenditure; FitAI uses Mifflin–St Jeor.

Hypertrophy — Muscle growth from training, protein, and rest.

RIR — Reps in reserve before technical failure.

When should I weigh myself? First thing in the morning, before eating; track the 30-day trend.

Missed a workout? Continue with the next scheduled day; consistency over months matters.

Food logging accuracy? Within ~10% of targets is enough; log main protein and calorie sources.

Design and Brand OS: FitAI team. Engineering: Next.js, Supabase, Playwright, Vitest. Fonts: Sora and DM Sans via Google Fonts.
